properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. The second half of Anthony's 2026-08-17 topic, separated from `dec:idea-can-a-design-hold-the-external-premise-it-rests-on` because that asks for something reflow2 CANNOT do and this asks why what it CAN do is never done.

HIS SCENARIO, verbatim: "increment 1 built to requirements A,B,C; but in increment 2, requirement A is no longer valid (it has been retired) and requirement D has been added." He suspected it might already fit inside epochs and increments. IT LARGELY DOES, and that is worth saying plainly before anything is designed:

WHAT IS ALREADY BUILT AND WORKING —
• `arrival_delta(epoch_or_release)` answers his question almost exactly. Its own description: "what didn't we achieve that we were supposed to in increment 10?" Five outcomes per item: `delivered`, `deferred` (still intended, date moved, and WHERE TO), `discontinued` (no longer intended at all), `outstanding` (still pointed here and NOBODY HAS SAID which — the question to put to the user, never to default). **Work scheduled AFTER the baseline is reported separately**, which is requirement D. So A-retired shows as `discontinued` and D-added shows as post-baseline work.
• Retirement is recorded properly. MEASURED: 13 retired requirements (9 dropped, 4 deferred), and every one of the 9 carries GOVERNED_BY (a Decision saying why), CHANGED (a ChangeEvent) and HAS_SNAPSHOT (the prior state). The `retire-from-design` skill forces the one question that matters — "was this ever true?" — because history is retired on the record while a mistake is deleted.

⚠️⚠️ WHAT IS BUILT AND NEVER TOUCHED. MEASURED 2026-08-17 across 176 requirements and 9,920 edges:
    Requirement `lineage`   176 of 176 `original`. `derived` 0. `decomposed` 0.
    EVOLVES_INTO            0 edges
    SUPERSEDES              0 edges
    SUPPLEMENTS             0 edges
⇒ THE GRAPH CANNOT SAY THAT D REPLACED A, and not because it lacks the words. `EVOLVES_INTO` and `SUPERSEDES` are declared edge types; `lineage: derived` is a declared value with real semantics attached.

⭐⭐ AND THE DECIDING MEASUREMENT WAS TAKEN RATHER THAN LEFT AS A SUGGESTION. An earlier draft of this node said the countable question — did the 9 dropped requirements actually HAVE successors? — was "worth testing before any of it" and that nobody had counted it. Counted, same day:

    dropped requirements whose reason-text NAMES a replacement:  9 OF 9

Every one reads "FOLDED INTO `req:defaults-do-not-assert`" — a real, live requirement, named explicitly, in prose, with ZERO `SUPERSEDES` edges anywhere in the graph. (One bulk retirement act across nine requirements rather than nine independent judgements, which does not soften it: the successor was known at the moment of retirement in every case.)

⇒ SO OPTION (D) IS DEAD. The zero is not an honest description of a design where nothing replaced anything; it is a design where the replacement was known, written down, and written down in the ONE FORM THE GRAPH CANNOT QUERY. Ask "what replaced `req:blocking-is-partial`?" and the answer requires a human to read a paragraph. That is the same failure as every other finding in this increment — the information exists and the structure does not, so it cannot be counted — and it is `req:a-finding-has-somewhere-to-put-its-evidence` arriving through a third door.

⇒ AND IT IS A WORKFLOW GAP, NOT A VOCABULARY GAP, which the count now supports rather than merely suggesting. The words existed, the author knew the answer, and no moment in the loop asked for it: not `capture-intent`, not `retire-from-design`, not `plan-increments`. Adding vocabulary here would produce another unused field.

THE SHAPES, none chosen:
(A) ASK AT RETIREMENT. `retire-from-design` already forces "was this ever true?"; add "is something taking its place?" — one question, at the moment the answer is demonstrably known, and the measurement says it would have been answered 9 times out of 9.
(B) ASK AT CAPTURE. `capture-intent`'s search-before-you-add already surfaces near matches and forces a choice between sharpen and `distinct_from`; a third option — SUPERSEDES — catches the replacement where the duplicate guard is already looking.
(C) COMPUTE AND OFFER. A retirement whose reason-text names another node id is a candidate supersession, reported as a question and never asserted (`dec:ask-not-repair`). On this corpus that alone would recover all nine.
(D) ~~LEAVE IT~~ — RULED OUT by the measurement above.

📌 THE CHEAPEST NEXT MOVE IS PROBABLY (A) PLUS (C): ask going forward, and offer the nine already sitting in prose as candidates for the user to confirm. Neither asserts anything.

properties.rationale: Recorded as brainstorming. His scenario is largely already built — arrival_delta reports discontinued-versus-delivered per increment and reports post-baseline additions separately. What is missing is genealogy, and the deciding measurement was taken rather than left as a suggestion: all 9 dropped requirements NAME their successor in prose ("FOLDED INTO req:defaults-do-not-assert") while zero SUPERSEDES edges exist. So the words existed, the author knew the answer, and no moment in the loop asked for it — a workflow gap, and the "leave it" option is ruled out.
